entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Faustinus of Brescia (fl. 4th century) was the bishop of Brescia from approximately 360 CE, succeeding Ursicinus and preceding Gaudentius I.

As the bishop of Brescia, Faustinus played a significant role in the religious and political landscape of the Roman Empire during the late 4th century. He was instrumental in shaping the theology and practices of the Catholic Church, particularly with regards to the sacraments and the role of the bishop.

Faustinus's significance extends beyond his individual achievements, as he represents a key figure in the transmission of Christian doctrine and practice from the apostolic era to the early Middle Ages. His feast day is celebrated on 15 February in the Roman Catholic Church and on 16 February in the Orthodox Church.

The legacy of Faustinus can be seen in the numerous writings attributed to him, including homilies, letters, and treatises on theology and spirituality. These works provide valuable insights into the theological debates and controversies of the time, offering a unique window into the intellectual and cultural currents of late antiquity.

Despite his relatively minor status among the bishops of the Western Roman Empire, Faustinus's influence can be detected in the writings of later theologians and Church Fathers, such as Jerome and Augustine.

One striking statistic that highlights the significance of Faustinus is the number of bishoprics he oversaw during his tenure. As the bishop of Brescia, he was responsible for the governance of a significant portion of the Western Roman Empire's ecclesiastical landscape, underscoring his importance as a key figure in the transmission of Christian doctrine and practice.
